0.original: Wuk Lamat wishes to know how traversable the Ty'iinbek Traverse is.

28.original: Use the pairing stone on the glowing rock.

48.original: For as weathered as our Promise looks, she's positively glowing with confidence. What in the world happened?

49.original: The twins ran me from one end of the Ut'ohmu Horizon to the other, asking about everything of remote interest along the way...

50.original: Erenville's tour was both educational and exciting! I hope we can persuade him to conduct another in the lower forests.

51.original: Did something happen while we were away? There's a certain satisfied air about you...

52.original: So what's the state of the Ty'iinbek Traverse?

53.original: Still being cleared, I'd assume. Hunmu Rruk said he would notify us as soon as work was done.

54.original: Then perhaps now would be a good time to consider how we might reclaim Wuk Lamat's stolen keystone. The next feat will be our last, after all.

55.original: Oh, I already got it back.

57.original: Not to mention how! This is Bakool Ja Ja we're talking about!

58.original: ...So I taught him a lesson and took my keystone back.

59.original: You bested Bakool Ja Ja in single combat? Bravo!

60.original: Hehe, what can I say? I've had good friends to encourage and cheer me on.

61.original: There you are. Our excavators have contacted me with news of their success. The Ty'iinbek Traverse is now safe for travel.

62.original: Then we finally can make for Mamook.

63.original: Come to think of it, isn't it Bakool Ja Ja's home? We can only hope its residents don't share his winning personality.

64.original: If it is indeed the city where Ketenramm first met the Dawnservant, surely some civility awaits us.

65.original: I would not be so certain.

66.original: It is true that the Dawnservant received Ketenramm in Mamook and was instrumental in the establishment of friendly relations between the Xbr'aal and Mamool Ja.

67.original: But since that time, most of the Mamool Ja who supported his peace have left their city in favor of abiding in the capital.

68.original: What remains is a cloister of Mamook. And while these traditionalists do not take up arms against us, neither do they bear great love for outsiders.

69.original: Whatever they're like, the people of Mamook are also of Tuliyollal. If I'm to be Dawnservant, it's my job to know them first of all.

70.original: Well, we'll be on our way, then. I'm glad I could learn about where I came from. And eat so much xibruq pibil besides!

71.original: Thank you for everything, Hunmu Rruk. Till next time, take care!

72.original: First we make our way across the Xobr'it Cinderfield, due southeast.

74.original: I filled my bag with xibruq pibil before we left, but I'm down to my last serving already...

75.original: I wonder if the First and Second Promises have already arrived in Mamook.

76.original: If Bakool Ja Ja ran in this direction after losing to Wuk Lamat, then he undoubtedly was returning to Mamook.

77.original: After seeing that battlefield, I find it miraculous that the Dawnservant was able to negotiate a peace.

78.original: The Traverse will bring us straight into the Ja Tiika Heartland.

79.original: ...Remember how you insisted this forest is green?

80.original: This path is quite steep, isn't it? Let us take our time and descend safely.

83.original: I'll take a moment's rest, I think...

84.original: I spoke with one of the excavators on my way down. Apparently, Bakool Ja Ja cleared away the one fallen tree remaining by barreling through it.

85.original: That Wuk Lamat single-handedly defeated someone possessed of such physical might is nothing short of remarkable.

86.original: Still, we ought to proceed with caution. There's no telling what his wounded pride might compel him to attempt.

87.original: We will doubtless face Bakool Ja Ja again. I cannot say I relish the thought of the reunion.

88.original: Erenville said this Traverse was dug to facilitate incursions into the forests above. Intentions notwithstanding, you have to admire the dedication.

90.original: Just look at this thing! What a vibrant glow!

92.original: In more ways than one. Take my pairing stone and hold it close to the glowing rock.

93.original: Go on. Use my pairing stone and see what happens.

94.original: As you hold the pairing stone in the soft glow, it affixes itself to the boulder with surprising force.

95.original: Pairing stones are natural magnets─and that's a meteorite filled with iron. One of many remnants of an ancient meteor shower.

96.original: The heterogeneous aether they emit causes surrounding flora to glow unique hues, as you can see.

97.original: So these glowing boulders came plummeting down from the heavens? Vidraal be merciful...

100.original: A far cry from the upper forests, indeed.

101.original: This place is already so fascinating... I'm eager to hear what the people of Mamook can tell us about it!

103.original: Now to see whether or not Hunmu Rruk's fears were well founded...

104.original: Rather more quiet than I expected...

105.original: I wonder what the final feat will be.

106.original: And here we finally are... Now to find the elector!

107.original: As this is also my first time visiting Mamook, I have no experience interacting with the locals.

108.original: But given Hunmu Rruk's parting words, I would advise...a cautionary approach.
